MORNING MONEY
Fed week, your card

lines.text: Every economist in a Reuters poll, 100 of 100, sees a December rate hike.
lines.say: Every economist in a Reuters poll sees a December rate hike.

lines.text: But for Wednesday's Fed decision, 94 of 100 expect no change.
lines.say: But for Wednesday's Fed decision, ninety-four of a hundred expect no change.

lines.text: Here's why it matters. In September, the Fed made its first hike since 2023, to 3.75% to 4%.
lines.say: Here's why it matters. In September, the Fed made its first hike since twenty twenty-three, to three point seven five to four percent.

lines.text: The next day, big banks lifted their prime rate from 6.75% to 7%.
lines.say: The next day, big banks lifted their prime rate from six point seven five to seven percent.

lines.text: Most credit cards have variable rates built on prime plus a margin, so card rates rose too.
lines.say: Most credit cards have variable rates built on prime plus a margin, so card rates rose too.

lines.text: Example: on a $5,000 balance, each quarter-point hike adds about $12.50 a year.
lines.say: For example, on a five thousand dollar balance, each quarter-point hike adds about twelve dollars and fifty cents a year.

lines.text: Card balances and home equity lines usually feel it, but fixed-rate loans you already have don't change.
lines.say: Card balances and home equity lines usually feel it, but fixed-rate loans you already have don't change.

lines.text: So the dates to watch are Wednesday at 2 p.m. Eastern, and then December 9.
lines.say: So the dates to watch are Wednesday at two p.m. Eastern, and then December ninth.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Reuters poll: all 100 see a Dec Fed hike. Your card?
post.ig:
Every economist in a Reuters poll, 100 of 100, sees a December rate hike.
For the Fed decision on Wednesday, Oct 28, 94 of 100 expect no change from 3.75%-4.00%.
The Fed raised rates Sept 16, its first hike since 2023, and big banks lifted the prime rate from 6.75% to 7.00% on Sept 17.
Most credit cards have variable rates built on prime. Example: on a $5,000 balance, each quarter-point hike adds about $12.50 a year.
Sources: Reuters poll (Oct 20, 2026), Federal Reserve, CNBC, U.S. Bancorp, Wells Fargo.
News and education, not financial advice.
